answer: An agent selling a falcon count from a ledge or a yarrow survey can claim cooperative grants only through an operator credential issued at a synchronized in-person enrollment. One attendee receives one credential, and all delegated agents share its grant quota. Overlapping sessions prevent one person from touring venues; 100 grant identities require recruiting 100 people and paying their travel and time. Organizers must prevent repeat entry and colluding issuers. Credential rental remains possible, so the scheme raises recruitment costs without proving each agent is independent.
